newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa market looks to grind, arrival data.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa market looks to grind, arrival data.

text.p: German cocoa bean buyers were absent from the market where the focus had shifted to await forthcoming third quarter cocoa grind data and news on new Ivorian crop supply, traders said on Wednesday.
"Futures are range-bound and sterling is unattractively high versus the other European currencies," one said.
"That deters consumers...but in retrospect, it may well be a wise time to buy now, before either high grind figures or slow progress in West Africa lifts prices," he believed.
Traders generally expected higher cocoa grindings in all consumption centres, including the U.S.
This would at least underpin the existing price floor.
The figures will be released in first-half October.
British grind figures were seen unchanged to as much as 10 percent up, analysts said earlier today.
Traders noted potential underlying demand from chocolate manufacturers, who were busy producing for the Christmas and Easter seasons in late December and April 1997.
"But they're living of old contracts...we're still waiting for new bean business," said one trader.
In Ivory Coast, where the 1996/97 marketing season starts on October 15, cocoa was on its way to port warehouses, according to reports received here, he said.
"It would be ready for shipment at that date, but it will come down to whether or not the Caisse (de Stabilisation) wants to encourage, or delay, the export process."
Local bean prices were unchanged from last week 2.27-2.31 marks/kg in the fourth quarter.
The 1996 cocoa butter ratio remained at 2.84 and implied cocoa butter prices liquid ex-works were steady at 6.55-6.59 marks.
London Dec futures were unchanged at 1130 GMT at 985 stg. Sterling was around 2.35 versus the mark compared with roughly 2.30 two weeks ago. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
